memory_update.text: The Restaurants theme currently maps most strongly to foodservice distribution and franchise supply-chain orchestration, where route density, procurement breadth, ordering infrastructure, food-safety resources, and SKU standardization can matter more than consumer-facing restaurant traffic alone.

Specialty foodservice distribution is the strongest underfollowed public-market node identified so far; Chefs' Warehouse and HF Foods show how restaurant exposure can be hidden inside specialty, ethnic, or fragmented distributor categories.

Franchise supply-chain orchestration should remain a core node; National DCP is a private/reference example showing how sourcing, distribution, restaurant solutions, and limited-time-offer execution support quick-service restaurant systems.

Layer 1C universe remains too narrow across the full Restaurants theme; next searches should add packaging, protein, beverage/coffee inputs, sanitation/QA, cold-chain/refrigeration, pest control, software, and testing/inspection candidates.
Future Layer 1 expansion should prioritize USD 300M-10B small/mid-cap suppliers with direct filing evidence of restaurant or foodservice exposure and low analyst/media mindshare.

summary: Layer 1C merged the available Layer 1A/1B evidence into a deduplicated initial Restaurants universe. The current evidence set is heavily weighted toward foodservice distribution and franchise supply-chain orchestration, with Sysco, US Foods, Performance Food Group, Chefs' Warehouse, and HF Foods forming the strongest mapped node. The highest Serenity relevance comes from companies controlling route density, procurement breadth, specialty SKU access, restaurant customer relationships, franchise-readiness infrastructure, and quality/food-safety execution. The universe is still narrow because Layer 1B evidence for packaging, protein processors, beverage suppliers, sanitation/QA, refrigeration/cold-chain, restaurant software, and testing/inspection was not fully available in the provided context. Underfollowed names are retained where they have clear restaurant-infrastructure exposure or a hidden signal to verify, even if later validation is required.
